title: Organise, present and interpret

blocks.heading: Organise, present and interpret
blocks.text: Organise records consistently, reconcile totals, then choose a suitable graph or sketch map to answer the enquiry. A table states observations; interpretation links relevant evidence into a pattern. Percentage equals category count divided by the relevant total, multiplied by 100; identify missing data and avoid asserting causation from association alone.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Findings
blocks.text: Findings report and interpret collected evidence, including comparisons and exceptions relevant to the aim. A high value differs from a large increase. Use paired observations and units rather than a list with no relationship.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Graphs
blocks.text: Bar charts compare categories; pie charts or divided rectangles show parts of a stated whole when categories are compatible. For bars state axes, units, category labels and an even scale. Pie angle is category share multiplied by 360°; a divided rectangle allocates proportional lengths. Totals must reconcile. Graphs here use data and construction specifications, not an unseen verified rendering.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Sketch maps
blocks.text: A sketch map locates relevant features and patterns using clear symbols and a key, title and orientation. Use observed or supplied relative positions; do not imply accurate scale unless measured. Distinguish a spatial pattern from a graph of category totals.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: An original observation table records 3, 6 and 5 users in three named waiting-time categories. A bar graph gives the categories on the horizontal axis and users on a labelled vertical scale from zero; separated equal-width bars show heights 3, 6 and 5. A title, time period and source identify what is represented. The middle category is largest, but the graph alone does not explain why.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Check representation by construction
blocks.text: For a separate worked pie example, 20 journeys comprise 8 walking, 7 cycling and 5 using a bus. Their sector angles are 144°, 126° and 90°: divide each count by 20 and multiply by 360°. The angles total 360°. For production-cost shares of 50%, 30% and 20%, a 15 cm divided rectangle has sections 7.5, 4.5 and 3 cm, with boundaries at 7.5 and 12 cm. Label the whole, categories and period. A separate sketch-map example has a north–south road, a clinic at its north end, a bus stop midway and a reading room east of its south end; use symbols, a key, orientation and title, without implying measured scale. A research-process flow chart links question, planning/ethics, pilot, collection, presentation and conclusion; a pilot decision can loop back to revision. Arrows show procedure, not quantities. These specifications do not verify an unseen plotted figure.
